title: Germany's BSI raises its cyber threat rating to "tense to critical" in annual report
summary: Germany's BSI raised its assessment of the threat to IT systems to "tense to critical" in its annual report, up from "tense" last year, according to Reuters as carried by Insurance Journal. The report said the threat took a "critical turn" in the current period. It reported its BSI Cyber Index at 238 points at mid-year, up from 124 at the same point in 2025.
plain: Germany's cyber agency now rates the threat to IT systems as "tense to critical", up from "tense" a year earlier, and says its new cyber index has risen sharply.
exec: Germany's cyber agency reports a worse threat rating than last year, with its BSI Cyber Index at 238 points at mid-year, up from 124 a year earlier.

evidence.quote: BSI Cyber Index: 238 points at mid-year, up from 124 at the same point in 2025.

validation.note: Two publishers read, each stating the 'tense to critical' rating: Insurance Journal (Reuters) and 24-ore.com. BSI's own page was not read. 24-ore.com says the index peaked at 238 points in Q2 2026.

review.note: Compared title, date 19 Nov, last year's 'tense', 238 and 124 figures against Insurance Journal (Reuters); 24-ore.com states the same rating
